page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile characterized by moderate memory throughput and constrained CPU compute power. The instance achieves average performance in large-block uncached memory read and write operations, as well as in Redis SET operations and Passmark CPU tests. However, single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests falls into the bottom 25%, with single-threaded compression and decompression tasks ranking in the bottom 10%. This indicates a tradeoff where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.2xlarge offers a high density of memory resources relative to its compute allocation, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not demand high-frequency CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include in-memory caching layers like Redis, medium-sized database deployments, and memory-intensive background processing tasks that can operate within the 2 Gbps network baseline.
